ex.en: Hackers are adept at getting around computer security measures.
ex.zh: 駭客很擅長繞過電腦的安全措施。

ex.en: Hackers find new ways of infiltrating private or public networks.
ex.zh: 駭客不斷找到入侵私人或公共網路的新方法。

ex.en: Many people cannot understand the way hackers behave.
ex.zh: 很多人無法理解駭客的行為。

ex.en: The transition from hardware to software happened gradually.
ex.zh: 從硬體轉向軟體的轉變是逐步發生的。

ex.en: We need to upgrade our computer hardware.
ex.zh: 我們需要升級電腦硬體。

ex.en: I bought some nails at the hardware store.
ex.zh: 我在五金行買了一些釘子。

ex.en: The hardware store sells paint and tools.
ex.zh: 五金行有賣油漆和工具。

ex.en: Smoking is harmful to your health.
ex.zh: 吸菸有害健康。

ex.en: Some medicines can be harmful to the body.
ex.zh: 有些藥物可能對身體有害。

ex.en: This medicine doesn't have any harmful side effects.
ex.zh: 這種藥沒有有害的副作用。

ex.en: That's very handy.
ex.zh: 這很方便。

ex.en: This app is really handy for booking taxis.
ex.zh: 這個 App 叫計程車很方便。

ex.en: It really comes in handy.
ex.zh: 這真的很能派上用場。

ex.en: A flashlight will come in handy if the power goes out.
ex.zh: 停電時手電筒就能派上用場。

handy.zh: 就在手邊的、隨手可得的

ex.en: I'll keep this information handy for future reference.
ex.zh: 我會把這份資料放在手邊，方便日後參考。

ex.en: Keep your passport handy at the airport.
ex.zh: 在機場時把護照放在隨手拿得到的地方。

ex.en: She is handy with a needle.
ex.zh: 她很會做針線活。

ex.en: Tom is handy with tools.
ex.zh: 湯姆很會用工具。

ex.en: Hazardous materials must be stored safely.
ex.zh: 危險物品必須安全存放。

ex.en: Smoking is hazardous to your health.
ex.zh: 吸菸有害健康。

ex.en: Driving in this fog is hazardous.
ex.zh: 在這種濃霧中開車很危險。

ex.en: He is a habitual smoker.
ex.zh: 他是個老菸槍。

ex.en: She ordered her habitual cup of black coffee.
ex.zh: 她照例點了一杯黑咖啡。

ex.en: The hallway needs to be wide enough for a wheelchair.
ex.zh: 走廊要夠寬，輪椅才過得去。

ex.en: The restroom is at the end of the hallway.
ex.zh: 洗手間在走廊盡頭。

ex.en: Please don't leave boxes in the hallway.
ex.zh: 請不要把箱子放在走廊上。

ex.en: Can I have two hamburgers and a coke, please?
ex.zh: 請給我兩個漢堡和一杯可樂，謝謝。

ex.en: Please give me a hamburger.
ex.zh: 請給我一個漢堡。

ex.en: Most Americans like hamburgers.
ex.zh: 大多數的美國人喜歡漢堡。

ex.en: Wet floors are a safety hazard.
ex.zh: 濕滑的地板有安全上的危險。

ex.en: Smoking is a serious health hazard.
ex.zh: 抽菸會嚴重危害健康。

ex.en: Can you hazard a guess at the price?
ex.zh: 你能猜猜看價格是多少嗎？

ex.en: I'd hazard a guess that he's over fifty.
ex.zh: 我猜他應該超過五十歲了。

ex.en: Please read the employee handbook before your first day.
ex.zh: 請在上班第一天前讀完員工手冊。

ex.en: The handbook explains the company's leave policy.
ex.zh: 手冊裡說明了公司的請假規定。

ex.en: He's even more hardworking than you are.
ex.zh: 他比你還要勤奮。

ex.en: She is one of the most hardworking people on our team.
ex.zh: 她是我們團隊裡最勤奮的人之一。

ex.en: Our hardworking staff deserve a bonus.
ex.zh: 我們辛勤的員工值得獲得獎金。

ex.en: Only a handful of people know the fact.
ex.zh: 只有少數幾個人知道真相。

ex.en: Only a handful of customers complained.
ex.zh: 只有少數幾位顧客抱怨。

ex.en: He grabbed a handful of rice.
ex.zh: 他抓了一把米。

ex.en: Tom bent down and picked up a handful of sand.
ex.zh: 湯姆彎下腰，抓起一把沙。

ex.en: My two-year-old son is a real handful.
ex.zh: 我兩歲的兒子很難帶。

ex.en: The new intern is a bit of a handful.
ex.zh: 新來的實習生有點難搞。

halt.zh: 停止、中止（常用 come to a halt）

ex.en: As the train came to a halt, all of the passengers wondered what was happening.
ex.zh: 列車停下來時，所有乘客都想知道發生了什麼事。

ex.en: Production came to a halt because of the power outage.
ex.zh: 因為停電，生產全面停擺。

ex.en: The company halted production after the accident.
ex.zh: 事故發生後，公司停止了生產。

ex.en: The government halted the project because of safety concerns.
ex.zh: 政府因安全疑慮叫停了這項計畫。

ex.en: There has been a good apple harvest this year.
ex.zh: 今年蘋果的收成很好。

ex.en: We're expecting a good harvest this year.
ex.zh: 我們期待今年有好收成。

ex.en: There was a large harvest of peaches last year.
ex.zh: 去年桃子大豐收。

ex.en: Farmers harvest the rice in October.
ex.zh: 農夫在十月收割稻米。

ex.en: The tea leaves are harvested by hand.
ex.zh: 這些茶葉是手工採收的。

ex.en: The company sold ten million handsets last year.
ex.zh: 這家公司去年賣出一千萬支手機。

ex.en: Pick up the handset and dial 9 for an outside line.
ex.zh: 拿起話筒，撥 9 可以打外線。

ex.en: My manager's criticism was harsh but fair.
ex.zh: 經理的批評很嚴厲，但很中肯。

ex.en: Don't be so harsh on yourself.
ex.zh: 別對自己太苛刻。

ex.en: I am slowly adjusting to the harsh climate here.
ex.zh: 我正慢慢適應這裡嚴酷的氣候。

ex.en: These plants can't survive the harsh winter.
ex.zh: 這些植物撐不過嚴寒的冬天。

ex.en: We hauled the boxes up the stairs.
ex.zh: 我們把箱子拖上樓。

ex.en: The truck hauls goods across the country.
ex.zh: 這輛卡車在全國各地運送貨物。

haul.zh: 收穫量；（一批）贓物、戰利品

ex.en: The fishermen brought in a big haul today.
ex.zh: 漁夫們今天滿載而歸。

ex.en: Police found a large haul of stolen goods.
ex.zh: 警方查獲了一大批贓物。

haul.zh: for the long haul：長期地、做長期打算

ex.en: We're in this for the long haul.
ex.zh: 我們打算長期投入。

ex.en: The company is planning for the long haul.
ex.zh: 公司正在做長遠的規劃。

ex.en: A rabbit has long ears and a short tail.
ex.zh: 兔子有長耳朵和短尾巴。

ex.en: Do you have a minute?
ex.zh: 你有空一下嗎？

ex.en: Let's have lunch together.
ex.zh: 我們一起吃午餐吧。

ex.en: We have a meeting at ten.
ex.zh: 我們十點要開會。

ex.en: I have already sent the report.
ex.zh: 我已經把報告寄出去了。

ex.en: Have you ever been to Japan?
ex.zh: 你去過日本嗎？

ex.en: I have to finish this by Friday.
ex.zh: 我必須在星期五前完成這件事。

ex.en: You don't have to come if you're busy.
ex.zh: 你忙的話不一定要來。

ex.en: You had better get away from here at once.
ex.zh: 你最好馬上離開這裡。

ex.en: You had better check the address again.
ex.zh: 你最好再確認一次地址。

ex.en: My brother is holding a camera in his hand.
ex.zh: 我弟弟手裡拿著一台相機。

ex.en: I entered the room and shook hands with him.
ex.zh: 我走進房間，跟他握手。

ex.en: Tom folded the paper before handing it to Mary.
ex.zh: 湯姆把紙折起來後才遞給瑪麗。

ex.en: Tom handed the envelope full of cash to Mary.
ex.zh: 湯姆把裝滿現金的信封交給瑪麗。

ex.en: Can you give me a hand?
ex.zh: 你可以幫我一下嗎？

ex.en: Do you need a hand with that box?
ex.zh: 那個箱子需要幫忙搬嗎？

hand.zh: on the other hand：另一方面

ex.en: On the other hand, the price is higher.
ex.zh: 另一方面，價格比較高。

ex.en: The job pays well. On the other hand, the hours are long.
ex.zh: 這份工作待遇好，但另一方面工時很長。

ex.en: Please hand in your report by Friday.
ex.zh: 請在星期五前繳交報告。

ex.en: Did you hand in your homework?
ex.zh: 你交作業了嗎？

ex.en: Who can tell what will happen in the future?
ex.zh: 誰能預料未來會發生什麼事？

ex.en: No matter what happens, you must not give up.
ex.zh: 無論發生什麼事，你都不能放棄。

ex.en: What happened at the meeting?
ex.zh: 會議上發生了什麼事？

ex.en: I happened to be out when the call came.
ex.zh: 電話打來的時候，我剛好不在。

ex.en: Do you happen to know her number?
ex.zh: 你剛好知道她的電話號碼嗎？

ex.en: You work too hard these days. Aren't you tired?
ex.zh: 你這陣子工作太拚了，不累嗎？

ex.en: I think it necessary for you to study harder.
ex.zh: 我認為你需要更用功讀書。

ex.en: The difference is this: he works harder than you.
ex.zh: 差別在於：他工作比你努力。

ex.en: Chinese is not the hardest language in the world.
ex.zh: 中文不是世界上最難的語言。

ex.en: It's hard to find a good apartment in Taipei.
ex.zh: 在台北很難找到好的公寓。

ex.en: This bread is too hard to eat.
ex.zh: 這個麵包硬到沒辦法吃。

ex.en: The chair was hard and uncomfortable.
ex.zh: 那張椅子又硬又不舒服。

ex.en: Your camera is only half the size of mine.
ex.zh: 你的相機只有我的一半大。

ex.en: At last, John and Sue decided to cut the apple into halves.
ex.zh: 約翰和蘇最後決定把蘋果切成兩半。

ex.en: The bird was half the size of a hawk.
ex.zh: 那隻鳥只有老鷹的一半大。

ex.en: Half a million children still face malnutrition in Niger.
ex.zh: 在尼日仍有五十萬名兒童面臨營養不良。

ex.en: I waited for half an hour.
ex.zh: 我等了半個小時。

ex.en: The work is only half done.
ex.zh: 工作只完成了一半。

ex.en: I was half asleep when you called.
ex.zh: 你打來時我已經半睡半醒了。

ex.en: I don't care as long as you are happy.
ex.zh: 只要你開心就好。

ex.en: I am happy to have so many good friends.
ex.zh: 我很高興有這麼多好朋友。

ex.en: I am happiest when I am reading.
ex.zh: 我閱讀的時候最快樂。

ex.en: I'd be happy to help you with that.
ex.zh: 我很樂意幫你處理。

ex.en: We are happy to answer any questions.
ex.zh: 我們很樂意回答任何問題。

ex.en: Are you happy with the new design?
ex.zh: 你對新設計滿意嗎？

ex.en: The client wasn't happy with the delay.
ex.zh: 客戶對延誤不太滿意。

ex.en: I had my hair cut at a barber's shop.
ex.zh: 我在理髮店剪了頭髮。

ex.en: The girl wore a yellow ribbon in her hair.
ex.zh: 那女孩的頭髮上綁了一根黃絲帶。

ex.en: The hair dresser is cutting the hair with scissors.
ex.zh: 理髮師正在用剪刀剪頭髮。

ex.en: A very beautiful picture is hanging on the wall.
ex.zh: 牆上掛著一幅非常漂亮的畫。

ex.en: We hung a Christmas wreath on the front door.
ex.zh: 我們在前門掛了一個聖誕花圈。

ex.en: You can hang your coat over there.
ex.zh: 你可以把外套掛在那邊。

ex.en: Hang on, I need to go to the bathroom.
ex.zh: 等一下，我得去一下洗手間。

ex.en: Hang on a second, I'll get my manager.
ex.zh: 稍等一下，我去叫我的經理。

ex.en: Please don't hang up; I'll transfer your call.
ex.zh: 請不要掛斷，我幫您轉接。

ex.en: She hung up before I could explain.
ex.zh: 我還來不及解釋，她就掛電話了。

hang.zh: hang out / hang around：閒晃、一起玩

ex.en: Some people were hanging around at the entrance.
ex.zh: 有些人在入口處閒晃。

ex.en: Do you want to hang out this weekend?
ex.zh: 這週末要一起出去玩嗎？

ex.en: Tom could hardly hear what Mary was saying.
ex.zh: 湯姆幾乎聽不見瑪麗在說什麼。

ex.en: It hardly ever snows here in the winter.
ex.zh: 這裡冬天幾乎不下雪。

ex.en: I could hardly follow what Jane said in her speech.
ex.zh: 我幾乎聽不懂珍演講的內容。

ex.en: Hardly had we come home when it began to rain.
ex.zh: 我們一到家就下起雨來了。

ex.en: I had hardly sat down when the phone rang.
ex.zh: 我才剛坐下，電話就響了。

ex.en: I can say with certainty that he hates me.
ex.zh: 我可以確定他恨我。

ex.en: Bill hates that his father smokes heavily.
ex.zh: 比爾很討厭他父親菸抽得那麼兇。

ex.en: I hate getting up early on Mondays.
ex.zh: 我討厭星期一早起。

hate.zh: hate to：很不想、不好意思（做某事）

ex.en: I hate to bother you, but could you help me?
ex.zh: 不好意思打擾你，可以幫我一下嗎？

ex.en: I hate to say it, but you're wrong.
ex.zh: 我很不想這麼說，但你錯了。

ex.en: Tom hung his jacket in the hall closet.
ex.zh: 湯姆把夾克掛在玄關的衣櫃裡。

ex.en: Somebody is waiting for Tom in the hall.
ex.zh: 有人在大廳等湯姆。

ex.en: The restrooms are down the hall on the left.
ex.zh: 洗手間在走廊盡頭左邊。

hall.zh: 會堂、禮堂（city hall 市政府）

ex.en: The teacher assembled the students in the hall.
ex.zh: 老師把學生集合在禮堂。

ex.en: The number of the chairs in the hall is 80.
ex.zh: 禮堂裡有八十張椅子。

ex.en: I passed the city hall on my way to the station.
ex.zh: 我去車站的路上經過了市政府。

ex.en: Take off your hat when you enter a classroom.
ex.zh: 進教室時請脫帽。

ex.en: There were no hats in that store that fit me.
ex.zh: 那家店裡沒有適合我的帽子。

ex.en: I picked out a new hat at the store.
ex.zh: 我在店裡挑了一頂新帽子。

ex.en: I don't think that I have any bad habits.
ex.zh: 我不覺得自己有什麼壞習慣。

ex.en: He fell into the habit of keeping late hours.
ex.zh: 他養成了熬夜的習慣。

ex.en: I wish I could break the habit of smoking.
ex.zh: 真希望我能戒掉抽菸的習慣。

ex.en: This book will do more harm than good.
ex.zh: 這本書弊大於利。

ex.en: From my point of view, cars do more harm than good.
ex.zh: 在我看來，汽車弊大於利。

ex.en: Drinking more water won't do you any harm.
ex.zh: 多喝水對你沒有壞處。

ex.en: There is no need to be frightened. He won't harm you.
ex.zh: 不用怕，他不會傷害你的。

ex.en: Too much sun can harm your skin.
ex.zh: 曬太多太陽會傷害皮膚。

ex.en: The scandal harmed the company's reputation.
ex.zh: 這起醜聞損害了公司的聲譽。

ex.en: It goes without saying that money cannot buy happiness.
ex.zh: 不用說，金錢買不到幸福。

ex.en: All these things serve to add to our happiness.
ex.zh: 這些都能增添我們的幸福。

ex.en: To love and to be loved is the greatest happiness.
ex.zh: 愛人與被愛是最大的幸福。

ex.en: There are many ships in the harbor.
ex.zh: 港口裡有很多船。

ex.en: The boat was piloted safely into harbor.
ex.zh: 船被安全地引導入港。

harbor.zh: 懷有（想法、感情）；藏有、窩藏

ex.en: She still harbors doubts about the plan.
ex.zh: 她對這個計畫仍心存疑慮。

ex.en: Dirty towels can harbor bacteria.
ex.zh: 髒毛巾可能藏有細菌。

ex.en: Pollution is destroying the habitat of many birds.
ex.zh: 汙染正在破壞許多鳥類的棲息地。

ex.en: The zoo tries to recreate each animal's natural habitat.
ex.zh: 動物園努力重現每種動物的自然棲息地。

ex.en: We went halfway up the mountain.
ex.zh: 我們爬到了半山腰。

ex.en: I am halfway through this detective story.
ex.zh: 這本偵探小說我才看到一半。

ex.en: I'm halfway through my sandwich.
ex.zh: 我的三明治吃了一半。

ex.en: We stopped at the halfway point to rest.
ex.zh: 我們在中途點停下來休息。

ex.en: By the halfway point of the year, sales had doubled.
ex.zh: 到了年中，銷售額已經翻倍。

ex.en: I'm willing to meet you halfway on the price.
ex.zh: 價格方面我願意跟你各退一步。

ex.en: If both sides meet halfway, we can reach a deal.
ex.zh: 如果雙方各讓一步，我們就能達成協議。

ex.en: The hawk caught a mouse.
ex.zh: 那隻老鷹抓到了一隻老鼠。

ex.en: One of the hawk's wings is broken.
ex.zh: 老鷹的一邊翅膀斷了。

ex.en: Vendors hawked souvenirs outside the temple.
ex.zh: 攤販在寺廟外叫賣紀念品。

ex.en: Street sellers were hawking umbrellas in the rain.
ex.zh: 下雨時街頭小販在兜售雨傘。

ex.en: Who did you hang out with last weekend?
ex.zh: 你上週末跟誰一起出去？

ex.en: Do you like hanging out with Tom?
ex.zh: 你喜歡跟湯姆一起出去玩嗎？

ex.en: I've been hanging out with him.
ex.zh: 我最近都跟他混在一起。

ex.en: Hang your clothes out to dry!
ex.zh: 把衣服拿出去晾乾！

ex.en: I hung the laundry out in the sun.
ex.zh: 我把洗好的衣服拿到太陽下晾。

ex.en: We haggled with the seller and got a better price.
ex.zh: 我們跟老闆殺價，拿到更好的價格。

ex.en: In some markets, haggling is expected.
ex.zh: 在有些市場，殺價是常態。

ex.en: They say this old house is haunted.
ex.zh: 據說老房子鬧鬼。

ex.en: I live in a haunted house.
ex.zh: 我住在一棟鬼屋裡。

ex.en: This old house is haunted.
ex.zh: 這個老房子鬧鬼。

ex.en: He was haunted by memories of the war.
ex.zh: 戰爭的回憶一直困擾著他。

ex.en: She had a haunted look in her eyes.
ex.zh: 她的眼神裡帶著揮不去的陰影。

ex.en: The two young girls smiled happily.
ex.zh: 兩個年輕的女孩高興地微笑了。

ex.en: He had no friends, no money, no home...but he played happily all the same.
ex.zh: 他沒有朋友，沒有錢，沒有房子……他照樣玩得很開心。

ex.en: I really hope they can live happily ever after as husband and wife.
ex.zh: 真的希望他們做夫妻白頭偕老。

ex.en: Years of war left the two groups full of hatred.
ex.zh: 多年的戰爭使這兩個族群充滿敵意。

ex.en: She looked at him with hatred in her eyes.
ex.zh: 她眼裡帶著恨意看著他。

ex.en: The company has a clear policy against workplace harassment.
ex.zh: 公司有明確的職場騷擾防治政策。

ex.en: Staff should report harassment to human resources.
ex.zh: 員工應向人資部門通報騷擾事件。

ex.en: The haulage company moved the equipment overnight.
ex.zh: 貨運公司連夜運送了這批設備。

ex.en: Haulage costs depend on distance and fuel prices.
ex.zh: 貨運費用取決於距離和燃料價格。

ex.en: Every worker must wear a harness at this height.
ex.zh: 在這個高度作業，每位工人都必須繫上安全吊帶。

ex.en: The inspector checked her harness before the climb.
ex.zh: 檢查員在她攀爬前檢查了安全吊帶。

ex.en: It is difficult for me to handle the case.
ex.zh: 這個案子我處理起來有困難。

ex.en: Tom should have handled the situation differently.
ex.zh: 湯姆當時應該用別的方式處理那個狀況。

ex.en: I’m still thinking how I’m going to handle this.
ex.zh: 我還在想要怎麼處理這件事。

ex.en: Here is a pan without handles.
ex.zh: 這是一個沒有把手的平底鍋。

ex.en: The door handle is broken.
ex.zh: 門把壞了。

ex.en: Please take a handout before the lecture begins.
ex.zh: 上課前請拿一份講義。

ex.en: The handout summarizes today's key points.
ex.zh: 這份講義整理了今天的重點。

ex.en: The farmers don't want handouts; they want fair prices.
ex.zh: 農民不要施捨，他們要的是合理的價格。

ex.en: The government announced cash handouts for low-income families.
ex.zh: 政府宣布發放現金給低收入家庭。

ex.en: Hold on a second, I'll be right back. Don't hang up!
ex.zh: 等一下，我馬上回來，不要掛斷！

ex.en: Please do not hang up the phone.
ex.zh: 請先不要掛上電話。

ex.en: I've got to hang up now. Someone is waiting to use the phone.
ex.zh: 我得掛電話了，有人在等著用電話。

ex.en: Hang up your coat, please.
ex.zh: 請把你的外套掛起來。

ex.en: Please hang up your jacket in the closet.
ex.zh: 請把外套掛在衣櫃裡。
